experiment: Structural search three-arm compile-only readout (the unmet Phase 1 gate): on rung 2 resume-projection-integrity and rung 4 pure-result-replay, from the direct seed with its coder rebound to Codex gpt-6.1-sol (I3: its matched typed Python workflow), do six completed topology-only episodes per interface (I3 matched Python diff, I1 Lisp whole-program, I2 Lisp locus-plus-fragment) collapse onto their parent, how local are their edits, and how do two accepted children per arm score in blind judging, reported descriptively per arm?
solutions: not recorded here: this file sits in the runtime agents can read; the operator passes each task's solution commit with --solution and the scan uses it
judge_note: score_codex.json binds only providers.judge (codex_unrestricted_workspace) and stays unchanged; the judge's model is score.orc's judge_model input, written from the judge's name (--judge gpt-6.1-sol=experiments/compare/providers/score_codex.json, E-B3's pattern)
parents_note: orc: the direct seed with providers.coder rebound to codex_unrestricted_workspace, model gpt-6.1-sol, effort high, archived as a new candidate (the frozen catalog seed is untouched), the parent of I1 and I2; python: its matched typed Python workflow (direct.py), the parent of I3, with the same adapter, model, effort and prompt

envelope.site_selection: uniform over eligible manifest sites, random.Random((run_seed, episode_index))
envelope.episode_environment: the mutator runs behind the shims with EPISODE.md on stdin, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and COMPARE_HIDE masking (bubblewrap mounts a tmpfs over each hidden directory after its --dev-bind / /, the episode's own tree bound back): the evidence root, sibling episodes, the work root's evaluation directories (records, runs, agents, env-manifests) and the operator's --hide roots, the Phase 1 roots among them; home stays readable and scan-detected
envelope.order: I1 rerun fresh (no Phase 1 episode reused); episodes one at a time; evaluations at concurrency 4

type_checker.name: pyright
type_checker.strictness: pyright default (basic) rules; errorCount must be 0; warnings do not refuse
type_checker.admission: acceptance.check_python: pyright on the entry module from the candidate root with a generated pyrightconfig.json (extraPaths the runtime the candidate runs with, enableTypeIgnoreComments false; PYTHONPATH dropped); accepted when errorCount is 0, else rejected type_check_failed with one diagnostic per error; pyright missing or exiting other than 0 or 1 raises
type_checker.suppression: a child whose entry module adds a comment silencing pyright (type: ignore, pyright: ...) that the parent lacks is rejected type_check_failed, rule suppression_comment
type_checker.parent: the parent must type-check clean against the runtime (acceptance.check_parent) or the run stops (RuntimeError): a runtime that does not resolve the frozen imports never rejects a child

i3.scope: acceptance.validate_python_scope: the mutable file's top level is frozen except the bodies of the mutable functions and added undecorated top-level functions; frozen_surface_changed for any other top-level change, a mutable function's changed parameters, return annotation or decorators, and inside the mutable or added functions a global/nonlocal or import statement, a store (or del) to a name bound at the parent's top level, a non-constant model=/effort= value or (topology-only) a model/effort constant new to the parent module; scope_exceeded for a removed mutable function, an added top-level node that is not an undecorated function, or any other file changed; declaration_collision for an added function named like a top-level name or a builtin
i3.planned_maximum: MAX_PROVIDER_CALLS = 8 per I3 child: the module's frozen runtime cap (ledger.python_call_cap) is the planned maximum its evaluations reserve; launches are reservation-aware: a launch waits for in-flight evaluations to settle and is refused only when it cannot fit under the cap with nothing in flight
i3.skeleton: records.python_skeleton_hash over the mutable functions only (mutable_definitions; added helper bodies excluded, as for I2); provider allocation from records.python_provider_allocation over the same functions
i3.prompt: the I3 parent sends the coder the ORC parent's prompt bytes once each clone's repo path is normalised; only the output contract's '- path:' line differs

collapse: per arm: collapsed when the terminal-only share of the arm's accepted children (skeleton and provider allocation both equal the parent's) exceeds collapse_threshold; children with the parent's skeleton but another allocation count as allocation_distinct, not as collapsed; unavailable without an accepted child
locality: an episode is out of scope when its verdict is scope_exceeded, frozen_surface_changed, digest_mismatch, site_unlocatable or declaration_collision; locality per arm = out-of-scope episodes over completed episodes (accepted + rejected), and files touched per episode from the final diff

subset.rule: accepted, uncontaminated, non-revisit children by episode index; the first; then the first later child with another skeleton; else the child with the smallest sha256(f'{subset_seed}:{candidate_id}') among the rest

primary_measure: the failure-inclusive blind rubric mean per task and arm: the mean over the arm's evaluations whose outcome is completed or failed, a completed evaluation contributing summarize's run value and a failed evaluation (the driver log's outcome field; collect records no patch for it, so summarize has no run row) 0 rubric points; incident evaluations are excluded and counted, and a completed evaluation without a value (excluded by summarize, e.g. contamination) is excluded and counted as excluded; read from results.json joined by scoring.join_scores and the task's failed and incident evaluations in the log (scoring.read_pool); arms are I3, I1 and I2, each over its subset children's evaluations; log rows count once per evaluation id (the last row, so a resumed incident counts as its later outcome); a timeout (an incident whose latest incidents entry shows 'launcher exit -9', scoring.scored_outcome) is a failure scored 0 and also reported apart. Reported descriptively per arm and per child: no separation decision; the Phase 1/Phase 2 decision stands
scale: each clone scores 0-8, the sum of score.orc's four rubric criteria (root_cause, scope, generality, layering), each 0-2, averaged over the judges not excluded; an evaluation's value is its final clone's (summarize's run value)
reported: per arm, never pooled across arms: completed episodes, acceptance per episode, locality and files touched per episode, distinct skeletons, revisit rate, exact repeats by program_digest, terminal-only share, allocation_distinct, collapsed
per arm and task: the subset children, mean (primary, failure-inclusive), valued_mean, failed, timeouts, incidents, excluded; per child its values per task
anchor scores per task and judge (summarize results.json); missing receipts are unavailable, never 0

budget.note: owner 2026-10-19: about 60 calls approved, cap 65 over smoke and main run (smoke roots separate; main run cap = 65 minus the smoke calls); the ledger reserves each launch's planned maximum and settles it to the shims' recorded calls; immediate zero-work refusals (exit within 2 s, no output) are listed, not charged

model_policy: every Codex call uses gpt-6.1-sol: the mutator, the rebound coder, the I3 coder and the OpenAI judge (owner, 2026-10-19); the Claude judge is claude-opus-5-5, also the model guard's default for any claude an agent starts; a Codex call's model is fixed by its argv; no call uses a Fable model (owner, 2026-10-15)
known_differences: I3's scope rule does not refuse direct subprocess or CLI calls, prompts written inline, ** splats, or calls that mutate frozen state (STATE.__init__(), PROVIDERS.update(...)); the shims record every provider call
the I3 and ORC parents' prompts differ only in the output contract's '- path:' line, once each clone's repo path is normalised
mutator isolation masks the named roots; home stays readable and the scan reads it
